quests.instruction: Spot the big hunter that needs a huge area to roam, because it has to find enough large prey to feed itself.
quests.hint: The bigger the meal, the further it has to travel to find one.
quests.explanation: Large predators need lots of space to find enough prey. A single tiger may roam over dozens of square kilometres.
quests.funFact: Tigers are mostly solitary, and each adult usually keeps its own territory.
quests.question: Tiger

quests.instruction: Which animal dries out quickly in the sun, so it hides in damp, shady places by day?
quests.hint: Its soft body loses water easily.
quests.explanation: Snails have soft, moist skin that dries out fast. They hide in cool, damp places and come out when it is wet.
quests.funFact: Snails often come out after rain, because wet ground is easier to glide across.
quests.question: Snail

quests.instruction: Spot the animal that keeps breathing holes open in the ice by scraping them with its teeth and claws.
quests.hint: It needs air, but ice is covering the water.
quests.explanation: Seals breathe air, so under the ice they keep breathing holes open. Some build snow dens above them to raise pups.
quests.funFact: Ringed seals build snow caves over breathing holes to keep their pups safe.
quests.question: Seal

quests.instruction: Which animal feeds close to its burrow, so it can dash underground at the first sign of danger?
quests.hint: It always stays near a safe hiding place.
quests.explanation: Rabbits stay near their burrow entrances. When a hunter appears, they sprint into the tunnel.
quests.funFact: A rabbit can swivel its ears to listen in different directions at once.
quests.question: Rabbit

quests.instruction: Which little ground-nesting bird flutters along as if its wing were broken, to lead a fox away from its nest?
quests.hint: It isn't really hurt. It's acting.
quests.explanation: A killdeer pretends to have a broken wing to draw a predator away from its eggs. Once the predator is far away, the bird flies off.
quests.funFact: A killdeer's speckled eggs blend in with the stones around the nest.
quests.question: Killdeer

quests.instruction: Pick the animals that swim in big, shiny groups, so a hunter has trouble picking out just one.
quests.hint: A crowd of swirling bodies confuses the hunter.
quests.explanation: When fish swim in a school, a predator can't easily pick out a single fish, which gives each fish a better chance of escaping.
quests.funFact: A school of fish can turn all at once, as if it were one animal.
quests.question: Fish

quests.instruction: Find the giant that helps forests grow by carrying seeds a long way inside its body and leaving them in its dung.
quests.hint: It eats fruit and then walks for many kilometres.
quests.explanation: Elephants eat fruits and travel far. The seeds pass through and are dropped in dung, which acts as a fertiliser.
quests.funFact: Some tree seeds sprout better after they pass through an elephant.
quests.question: Elephant

quests.instruction: Which tiny insect carries seeds underground to its nest, helping wildflowers spread?
quests.hint: The seeds have a tasty coating just for it.
quests.explanation: Some wildflower seeds have a tasty, oily coating. Ants carry them to their nests, eat the coating and leave the seed to sprout.
quests.funFact: Violets are one of the flowers that rely on ants to spread their seeds.
quests.question: Ant

quests.instruction: Which giant's droppings feed tiny sea plants, which helps the whole ocean food chain?
quests.hint: It feeds deep down and leaves its droppings near the surface.
quests.explanation: Whale droppings contain nutrients that help tiny floating sea plants grow. Those tiny plants feed many other animals.
quests.funFact: Tiny sea plants make a large share of the oxygen we breathe.
quests.question: Whale

quests.instruction: A scientist finds a skull with flat, grinding back teeth and no sharp fangs. Which animal could it belong to?
quests.hint: Flat teeth are made for crushing plants.
quests.explanation: Flat grinding teeth mean a plant-eater, like a horse. Lions and wolves have sharp teeth for meat.
quests.funFact: You can estimate a horse's age by looking at its teeth.
quests.question: Horse

quests.instruction: A neat grey pellet of fur and tiny bones lies beneath a tree. Which bird coughed it up?
quests.hint: It swallows its meal whole and sends back what it can't digest.
quests.explanation: Owls swallow small animals whole and later cough up the fur and bones they can't digest, in a neat pellet.
quests.funFact: Scientists can study owl pellets to find out exactly what an owl has been eating.
quests.question: Owl

quests.instruction: A stream bank has a tree stump with a pointed, pencil-like top. Which animal chewed it?
quests.hint: It gnaws all the way round, like a carpenter.
quests.explanation: Beavers gnaw all the way around a trunk until the tree falls, leaving a pointed, pencil-like stump.
quests.funFact: A beaver can fell a small tree in a single night.
quests.question: Beaver

quests.instruction: Find the sea animal that eats lots of jellyfish, even though they sting.
quests.hint: Its throat is lined with spines to keep slippery food from escaping.
quests.explanation: Leatherback turtles feed mostly on jellyfish. Spiny throats stop the slippery meal from sliding out.
quests.funFact: Floating plastic bags can look like jellyfish to a turtle, which makes them dangerous.
quests.question: Turtle

quests.instruction: Name the animal that eats mostly krill and small fish in cold seas.
quests.hint: It does its hunting underwater.
quests.explanation: Penguins feed on krill and small fish, which they chase underwater using their strong flippers.
quests.funFact: Penguins can swallow small fish underwater without coming up for air.
quests.question: Penguin

quests.instruction: Pick the basking reptile that eats mostly insects and spiders.
quests.hint: Its menu is mostly small, crunchy things.
quests.explanation: Many lizards eat insects and spiders, which they snap up quickly after warming in the sun.
quests.funFact: A lizard's sticky or quick tongue helps it grab its prey fast.
quests.question: Lizard

quests.instruction: 🐮 is grazing in a field. Which animal would be competing with it for the same grass?
quests.hint: It eats the same food in the same place.
quests.explanation: Animals that eat the same food in the same place are competitors. Sheep and cows both graze on grass.
quests.funFact: Sheep can graze grass closer to the ground than cows can.
quests.question: Sheep

quests.instruction: Find the grassland animal that tears off the tall, tough tops of the grass, leaving the softer parts for smaller grazers.
quests.hint: It goes first, and others follow.
quests.explanation: Zebras eat the tall, tough stems first. That leaves the shorter, softer grass for other grazers following behind.
quests.funFact: Zebras and wildebeest often travel together across the plains.
quests.question: Zebra

quests.instruction: Find the water bird that can reach plants deeper down than ducks, thanks to its long neck.
quests.hint: It feeds at a different depth from the others on the pond.
quests.explanation: A swan's long neck lets it reach plants deeper under the water, so swans and ducks can share a pond without competing as much.
quests.funFact: A swan can eat several kilograms of water plants in a day.
quests.question: Swan

quests.instruction: In a year with plenty of mice, which hunter is likely to have more babies that survive the next year?
quests.hint: More food means more families get fed.
quests.explanation: When there's plenty of prey, more young hunters like foxes get enough food to survive.
quests.funFact: Foxes can eat insects, fruit and small animals, so they don't depend only on mice.
quests.question: Fox

quests.instruction: A cold, wet spring kills many insects. Which small bird would struggle to feed its chicks?
quests.hint: Its chicks need a steady supply of insects.
quests.explanation: Many songbirds feed their chicks on insects, so if few insects survive the cold, the chicks may go hungry.
quests.funFact: Many songbird chicks leave the nest only two or three weeks after hatching.
quests.question: Songbird

quests.instruction: A farm drains the wetland beside it. Which animal that lays eggs in ponds would lose its breeding place?
quests.hint: Its eggs need still, shallow water.
quests.explanation: Frogs lay their eggs in water, so draining a wetland leaves them with nowhere to breed.
quests.funFact: In many places, wetlands are home to a huge variety of frogs, birds and insects.
quests.question: Frog

quests.instruction: Which of these gets its energy from the sun most directly, by eating plants and nothing else?
quests.hint: The others get their energy by eating other animals.
quests.explanation: A rabbit eats plants, which store the sun's energy. Foxes and owls get their energy from eating animals.
quests.funFact: Only a small part of the energy passes to the next animal at each step, so there are fewer hunters than prey.
quests.question: Rabbit

quests.instruction: Tiny sea plants feed small fish, which feed big fish. Which animal could be at the end of this chain?
quests.hint: It is the top hunter of the three.
quests.explanation: Sharks are large predators that eat big fish. Each link in the chain passes energy upward.
quests.funFact: Some sharks can sense a tiny amount of blood in the water from far away.
quests.question: Shark

quests.instruction: In a healthy grassland, which animal is likely to be the most numerous?
quests.hint: There is more food for plant-eaters than for meat-eaters.
quests.explanation: Energy shrinks at each step of a food chain, so there are far more plant-eaters than meat-eaters.
quests.funFact: A lion pride needs lots of prey animals to live on.
quests.question: Zebra

quests.instruction: A farmer has too many mice in the grain store. Which bird could help, if she puts up nest boxes for it?
quests.hint: It hunts at night, and mice are what it likes best.
quests.explanation: Barn owls eat lots of mice, so some farmers put up nest boxes for them. It's a natural way to control pests.
quests.funFact: A family of barn owls can eat thousands of mice in a year.
quests.question: Owl

quests.instruction: A fruit farmer wants more apples. Which flying helper should she welcome into her orchard?
quests.hint: It moves pollen from one blossom to another.
quests.explanation: Bees carry pollen from blossom to blossom. Without pollination many fruits don't form.
quests.funFact: Many of the foods we eat depend on pollinators like bees.
quests.question: Bee

quests.instruction: Where there are too few hunters, which animal can multiply and eat so many young trees that forests struggle to regrow?
quests.hint: It eats shoots and leaves, and there's no one to keep its numbers down.
quests.explanation: When there are few predators, deer can become too numerous and eat so many young trees that a forest can't regrow.
quests.funFact: Deer have no upper front teeth, so they tear plants rather than bite them off cleanly.
quests.question: Deer

quests.instruction: Which of these is hardly ever hunted once fully grown, because of its enormous size?
quests.hint: Few hunters dare to go near it.
quests.explanation: Adult elephants are so big that few predators will attack them, but calves are at risk. Herds protect the calves.
quests.funFact: When a herd feels threatened, elephants may form a circle around their calves.
quests.question: Elephant

quests.instruction: Name the animal that can live almost anywhere people do, because it eats almost anything and breeds quickly.
quests.hint: It's not fussy, and its family grows fast.
quests.explanation: Rats are adaptable omnivores that breed quickly, so they do well near people. Pandas and giraffes depend on specific foods.
quests.funFact: Rats are strong swimmers and can tread water for a long time.
quests.question: Rat

quests.instruction: When the rains fail and the grass dies, which animal is in the most trouble because it eats grass almost exclusively?
quests.hint: Its menu has one main item.
quests.explanation: Grass-eaters like bison suffer when grass dies. Omnivores like raccoons and bears can switch to other foods.
quests.funFact: Bison nearly disappeared in the 1800s, but their numbers have recovered with help.
quests.question: Bison
